name: CPS 234
appliesTo: APRA-regulated entities in Australia (ADIs, insurers, superannuation RSE licensees and related entities).
note: Paragraph-level mapping of the standard's requirements; APRA's guidance in CPG 234 is not mapped and the controls shown are indicative, not evidence of compliance.

requirements.title: Board ultimately responsible for information security
Define information security roles and responsibilities
Maintain information security capability commensurate with threats
Assess security capability of related and third parties
Actively maintain capability as vulnerabilities and threats change
Maintain information security policy framework commensurate with exposures
Policy framework directs responsibilities of all parties
Classify information assets by criticality and sensitivity
Implement controls proportionate to threats and asset criticality
Evaluate design of controls over third-party managed assets
Robust mechanisms to detect and respond to incidents
Maintain plans to respond to plausible incidents
Response plans cover incident stages and escalation
Annually review and test incident response plans
Systematic testing program for control effectiveness
Assess third-party control testing where relied upon
Escalate untimely-remediated control deficiencies to Board
Testing by skilled, functionally independent specialists
Review sufficiency of testing program annually or on change
Internal audit reviews design and effectiveness of controls
Internal audit staff have information security assurance skills
Internal audit assesses third-party control assurance
Notify APRA of material incidents within 72 hours
Notify APRA of material control weaknesses within 10 business days
